In re: An application for suspension of sentence under Section 389  (1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure/under Section 430(1) of the  BNSS filed on 28-03-2025.

-And-  In the matter of : Pabitra Singh @ Pabitra Singha  .... Appellant.

For the appellant.

Ms. Amita Gour,

For the State.

Dictated by Arijit Banerjee, J:-
 In Re : CRAN 1 of 2025:
 1.

By a judgment and order dated February 27, 2025, passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge,
5th Court, Howrah in Sessions Case No. 76 of 2019, the applicant was convicted for commission of offence under Section 376(1) of the Indian Penal Code and was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for ten years and to pay fine of Rs. 10,000/-.
The applicant has preferred appeal against the same and has filed the instant application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail pending disposal of the appeal.
2. The applicant says that defacto complainant is a major lady and a divorcee.
She on her own volition entered into relationship with the applicant.
There was no false promise made by the applicant to the defacto complainant.
In fact, the applicant has been acquitted of the charge under Section 417 of the IPC.
The applicant was on bail throughout the trial.
There is no real possibility of an early conclusion of the trial.
Even the paper books are not yet prepared.
The applicant should be granted bail on such condition as this Court may deem fit and proper.

sentences.text: Opposing the prayer, the learned Advocate for the State tells us that the applicant had meted out false promise to marry the defacto complainant.
The applicant entered into physical relationship with the defacto complainant on several occasions.
The evidence on record clearly implicates the applicant.
The medical report also corroborates the prosecution case.
Learned State Advocate strongly opposes the prayer for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
4. From the affidavit of service filed in court, we find that notice of this application has been received by the defacto complainant.
However, nobody appears for the defacto complainant.
5. We have considered the facts and circumstances of the case.
The victim lady is a major.
She was about 30 years of age at the relevant point of time.
The applicant was all along on bail.
It is nobody's case that the applicant jumped any condition of bail or abused/misused the privilege of bail.
There is also very little possibility of an early hearing of this appeal.
We find from a departmental note dated November 3, 2025 that trial court record has been received by the Department but the paper book is not ready.
The Department has asked for six weeks time to prepare paper books.

6. On an overall consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and on a prima facie assimilation of the evidence on record as also considering the fact that the applicant was on bail throughout the trial, we are inclined to allow the applicant's prayer for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
7.

Accordingly the appellant, namely, Pabitra Singh @ Pabitra Singha, shall be released on bail upon furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand), with two sureties of like amount each,
one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Howrah and on further condition that the appellant shall meet the Officer-in-Charge of the Kalna police station within the jurisdiction of which he resides, once a fortnight and further that the appellant shall be personally present or be represented before this Court when the appeal is taken up for hearing.
8. The operation of the order of conviction and sentence shall remain suspended till disposal of the appeal or until further orders, whichever is earlier.
We also stay the operation of payment of fine till disposal of the appeal.

9. The Department is directed to forward a copy of this order to the Superintendent of the concerned Correctional Home for immediate release of the applicant/appellant unless he is wanted in connection with any other case.

10. We clarify that the observations made by us in this order are only for the purpose of disposing of the application for suspension of sentence and the same shall have no relevance at the final hearing of the appeal.
11. The Department shall prepare requisite number of paper books within six weeks from date.
12. The application being IA No. CRAN 1 of 2025 is, thus, disposed of.
